title: Reflection & Refraction
hook: A straw looks bent in a glass of water — not because the straw bends, but because light does when it changes speed.
key_points: Reflection: light bounces off a surface, with the angle in equal to the angle out.
Refraction: light bends when it passes between materials where it travels at different speeds.
Light slows in denser media like water or glass, which bends its path.
Lenses and prisms work by carefully shaping refraction.
content_html: When light meets a boundary between two materials, two things can happen. Reflection bounces it back: a mirror sends light off at the same angle it arrived, which is why your reflection looks crisp. Refraction bends it: light that crosses into a new material — say from air into water — changes direction at the surface.
extra_html: Refraction happens because light travels at different speeds in different materials, slowing down in denser media like water or glass. That change in speed bends the path, the same way a car veers if one wheel hits mud. It's why a straw in a glass looks broken at the waterline and why a pool looks shallower than it is. Engineers exploit refraction deliberately: a lens is just a shaped piece of glass that bends incoming rays to a focus, and a prism bends different colors by different amounts to spread out a rainbow. HyperPhysics covers the geometry and the index of refraction behind it.

related.title: Is Light a Wave or a Particle?
related.hook: Light behaves like a wave in some experiments and like a stream of particles in others — and the surprising answer is that it's both.

flashcards.prompt: What causes light to refract when it enters water or glass?
flashcards.back_html: Light changes speed when it moves between materials; that change in speed bends its path. It slows in denser media like water or glass.

flashcards.prompt: For reflection off a flat surface, how do the incoming and outgoing angles compare?

choices.text: The angle in equals the angle out
The angle out is always twice the angle in
The angle out is always zero

flashcards.explanation_html: Reflection follows the law that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the surface's normal.

flashcards.prompt: Why does a straw look bent where it enters a glass of water?

choices.text: Light refracts at the water surface, shifting where the straw appears
The water physically bends the straw
Water absorbs the lower half of the straw

flashcards.explanation_html: Light from the submerged part bends as it leaves the water, so your eye sees it offset — the straw only looks bent.
